purpose: Maralixibat is used to treat a liver condition called Alagille syndrome, which causes bile to build up in the liver and leads to severe itching. It helps reduce the amount of bile acids in the body, which can relieve that intense, uncomfortable itching. It is approved for children 1 year and older with this condition.
how_it_works: Normally, bile acids made by your liver get reabsorbed back into your body from your intestines. Maralixibat works by blocking a protein in your intestines that does that reabsorption, so more bile acids leave your body through your stool instead of building back up. This lowers the overall level of bile acids in your blood, which helps reduce the itching caused by Alagille syndrome.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, stomach pain, vomiting, and loose stools. Some patients may also notice changes in liver blood test results. These side effects are usually mild to moderate but let your doctor know if they bother you or do not go away.
warnings: Maralixibat can cause liver problems, so your doctor will do regular blood tests to check how your liver is doing. If you notice yellowing of the skin or eyes, very dark urine, or unusual tiredness, contact your doctor right away. It may also cause diarrhea that leads to dehydration, especially in young children, so make sure your child stays well hydrated. Tell your doctor about all other medications your child takes, as this drug can interact with others.
typical_dosing: The dose is based on the child's body weight and is given once a day by mouth, usually in the morning. It comes as an oral liquid solution. Your doctor will calculate the right dose for your child and may adjust it over time. Always use the measuring device that comes with the medication to make sure you give the correct amount.
